program_overview.title: Data Analysis Mastery Course
program_overview.tagline: The honest analyst toolkit in the order jobs use it: Excel done properly, statistics and SQL, then Python, BI dashboards and the industry literacy that makes analysis land.
program_overview.description:
Data analyst is the most reachable serious tech role there is, and the job is concrete: take messy business data, make it trustworthy, and turn it into answers a decision-maker can act on. This live online course teaches exactly that craft in the order real work uses it: Excel to genuine mastery first, because it remains the language of business, with the statistics that keep analysis honest, then SQL to production analyst level including window functions, then the Python layer: Pandas for cleaning and transformation, real exploratory analysis, visualization, BI dashboards and data storytelling, plus practical machine learning for analysts. The third phase adds what bootcamps skip: industry literacy across finance, healthcare, retail, supply chain and HR analytics, cloud platforms, and the advanced statistical methods behind A/B tests. A finale month ships a portfolio capstone and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: about seven months of teaching at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with margin built in for revision and life. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.
what_makes_this_different: Excel respected, not skipped: business still speaks it, so analysts must own it
SQL to real analyst depth: joins, aggregation and window functions, not SELECT-star tutorials
Storytelling as a core skill: analysis that changes decisions, not chart dumps
Industry literacy included: finance, healthcare, retail, supply chain and HR analytics
An honest 8-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this data analysis course cover?
faqs.answer: The full analyst toolkit in working order: Excel to professional depth with the statistics that keep analysis honest, SQL including window functions, Python with Pandas for cleaning and exploratory analysis, visualization, BI dashboards, data storytelling and practical machine learning for analysts, then industry applications across finance, healthcare, retail, supply chain and HR, cloud analytics platforms and advanced statistical methods. A finale month ships a portfolio capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to become job-ready in data analysis?
faqs.answer: About seven months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with margin built in beyond that for learners who need it. Three phases build Excel with statistics and SQL, then Python with BI and storytelling, then industry applications; the finale month ships a portfolio capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Data analysis or data science: which course should I take?
faqs.answer: Ask what you want to do daily. Analysts answer business questions: cleaning data, writing SQL, building dashboards and telling the story, employable sooner and everywhere. Data scientists build models on top of that craft. This course makes you the first; our data science course continues into the second, and the skills stack rather than compete.

faqs.question: Do I need coding experience or strong maths?
faqs.answer: Neither. The course starts in Excel, where most professionals already live, and introduces SQL and Python step by step with practice after every class. The maths is the statistics an analyst genuinely uses, distributions, inference, A/B thinking, taught in plain language on real business data.
